_readme: Team-verified facts layered on top of NASA PSI metadata by scripts/build_atlas.py. Only add a value you can cite: put the citation in 'source'. Leave null if unknown - the app shows 'not curated yet' instead of guessing. O2 values are chamber/ambient mole fractions; pressures are in atm.

PSI-69.outcomes: Test end (Extinction/Disruption/Completion), burning-rate constant K, extinction diameter, burn time
PSI-69.notes: Diluents: N2, CO2 (up to 0.70), He (up to 0.45). Pressures above 1 atm occur only with ~70% CO2. Disruption outcomes may reflect needle-coating contamination (NASA/TP-2015-216046 sec. 5.2).
PSI-69.source: PSI-69_Experimental table_FLEX.csv inspected 2026-11-13; NASA/TP-2015-216046 Table IX

PSI-68.fuel_type: liquid fuel droplets (FLEX-2 fuels and blends)
PSI-68.outcomes: none tabulated: 8-row design-range table; raw logs and images only (~1.2 TB)
PSI-68.notes: O2 and pressure are DESIGN RANGES from the 8-row table, not per-test values.

PSI-159.fuel_type: gaseous fuel (e.g. ethane, propane, butane) from a spherical porous burner; normal and inverse flames
PSI-159.outcomes: Hot ignition (yes/no), burn time, self-extinguished vs flow-terminated, peak burner temperature, flame colour (inverse)
PSI-159.notes: Highest-oxygen microgravity tests in PSI: inverse flames flowed up to 85% O2 from the burner into a fuel/N2 chamber (challenge brief). 'Cool flame?' column filled only 8 times - not a usable label.
PSI-159.source: PSI-159 experimental tables (179 normal + 154 inverse rows) inspected 2026-11-13

PSI-10.fuel_type: gaseous fuel, spherical porous burner (normal and inverse flames)

PSI-20.fuel_type: gas burner that emulates burning solids (Burning Rate Emulator)
PSI-20.outcomes: day-level log only; per-test outcomes need raw files
PSI-20.notes: Ran ISS-like (14.7 psia/21% O2), 10.2 psia/26.5% O2 and exploration-like 8.2 psia/34% O2 atmospheres.

PSI-21.fuel_type: gaseous fuel, coflow laminar diffusion flames
PSI-21.outcomes: day-level rows only (18-32); 0.8-2 TB of raw data

PSI-22.fuel_type: gaseous fuel flames under an applied electric field (partial-gravity analogue)
PSI-22.outcomes: day-level rows only (18-32); 0.8-2 TB of raw data

PSI-23.fuel_type: gaseous fuel, spherical burner (structure and response of flames)
PSI-23.outcomes: day-level rows only (18-32); 0.8-2 TB of raw data

PSI-25.fuel_type: solid materials in forced airflow (e.g. PMMA, SIBAL fabric)
PSI-25.outcomes: chamber O2/CO2/CO before and after each burn; flame-spread rate only in videos/papers

PSI-26.outcomes: test matrix plus a 134-row 'as run' spreadsheet

PSI-98.fuel_type: large solid samples burned inside a departing Cygnus cargo vehicle
PSI-98.outcomes: sensor time series; too few samples for ML
PSI-98.notes: PSI lists dates 2001-2008 and platform ISS, which look copied from SAME; the description says Cygnus.

PSI-99.fuel_type: large solid samples burned inside a departing Cygnus cargo vehicle
PSI-99.outcomes: burn time; spread rate/length for some samples (n = 9)

PSI-100.fuel_type: large solid sample burned inside a departing Cygnus cargo vehicle
PSI-100.outcomes: sensor time series; too few samples for ML

PSI-101.fuel_type: spacecraft materials overheated to make smoke (5 materials)
PSI-101.outcomes: test matrix only; ISS/shuttle/ion detector + particle signals in 44 housekeeping CSVs (joinable per test)

PSI-102.fuel_type: spacecraft materials overheated to make smoke
PSI-102.outcomes: original SAME flight; see SAME-R for the reflight

PSI-47.fuel_type: dust/aerosol (no combustion) measured with SAME-type instruments

PSI-117.outcomes: digitized published results incl. cool-flame droplet extinction diameters (small CSV/xlsx)
